To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PAF is a sperm factor that may be involved in sperm-egg interactions; (2) PAF is present on the surface of the sperm head, where it may play a role in sperm-egg recognition; (3) PAF is involved in sperm-ovum fusion and in the acrosome reaction; (4) PAF is an important factor in sperm capacitation; (5) PAF may be involved in the process of fertilization; (6)
the addition of PAF to spermatozoa did not improve the IUI outcome, in a population of patients with mild male factor infertility.
(1) The use of PAF as a treatment for male infertility is not effective in unselected cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of platelet activating factor on sperm motility, sperm viability, sperm capacitation, and sperm binding to the zona pellucida.
the study of the role of platelet-activations factor (PAF) in the pathophysiology of human reproduction.
the development and application of new methods in the field of reproductive medicine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is not sufficient enough to support the claim that PAF treatment of sperm improves IUI outcome.
there is insufficient evidence that PAF treatment is beneficial in unselected cases with mild male factor infertility.
the use of PGE1 in the treatment of male infertility is not supported by evidence-based medicine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of PAF in the treatment of sperm prior to intrauterine inseminations in unselected cases with mild male factor infertility does not result in an improvement in clinical pregnancy rate.
we have demonstrated that PAF is a potent sperm activator and that it can be used to increase the motility of sperm in vitro.
we have demonstrated the presence of PAF in human spermatozoa, that PAF is present in the semen and that PAF is released during capacitation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spermatozoa of men with unexplained infertility have a reduced capacity to bind PAF and that this may be a cause for their infertility.
the use of platelet activating factor for sperm preparation prior to intrauterine inseminations does not improve pregnancy outcomes in patients with mild male factor infertility.
we need to be more careful in how we interpret and report the results from studies of sperm PAF.
